Jensen-Shannon centroid of categorical probability distributions.

Source: R/divergences_generic.R
jscent.Rd

jscent() is an S3 generic for computing the Jensen-Shannon centroid of R objects, with methods for the following classes:

  • igcmatcatdistn

Usage

jscent(p, weight = NULL, base = exp(1), tol = 1e-08, ...)

Arguments

p

An object of class igcmatcatdistn, i.e., a stochastic matrix (positive matrix with row sums equal to one).

weight

A vector of weights for the rows of p. Default is NULL, yielding uniform weights on the rows of p.

base

A positive value, the base of the logarithm to be used to compute Jensen-Shannon divergence. Default is exp(1).

tol

For igcmatcatdistn objects only. A positive value, the tolerance in the optimization procedure; see Details Section. Default is 1e-8.

...

Additionnal arguments for other methods.

Value

A positive numeric vector summing to one (object of class igccatdistn), i.e., a categorical probability distribution, approximation of the Jensen-Shannon centroid of the rows of p.

Details

If input p is a stochastic matrix (object of class igcmatcatdistn), the output is the probability distribution minimizing the weighted mean of Jensen-Shannon divergences with the rows of p. More precisely, let \(p_1, \cdots, p_n\) denote the rows of p and \(w_1, \cdots, w_n\) the components of the vector weight. The output of jscent() is a numerical approximation of the probability distribution \(p^*\) (object of class igccatdistn) satisfying $$p^* \in \textrm{Argmin} \left\{ \sum_{i=1}^n w_i \ \mathbb{JS}(p_i:q) \ | \ q >= 0, \sum_{x} q(x) =1 \right\},$$ where \(\mathbb{JS}(p_i:q)\) denotes the Jensen-Shannon divergence between \(p_i\) and \(q\); see jsdiv() for details.

This numerical approximation is obtained by the ConCave-Convexe Procedure (CCCP) introduced by Yuille and Rangarajan (2002), as stated in Nielsen (2020). It is an iterative optimization procedure for objective functions that can be written as the sum of two functions, one concave \(B\), the other convex \(A\). Starting from an initial pd \(p^{(0)}\) (the arithmetic centroid of rows of p), a sequence of pds \(p^{(1)}, \cdots, p^{(r)}\) is computed recursively through the formula $$p^{(t+1)} = (\nabla B)^{-1} \left( \nabla A (p^{(t)})\right), \quad t =1, \cdots, r,$$ where \(\nabla A\) and \(\nabla B\) denote gradients of functions \(A\) and \(B\). The algorithm stops as soon as the norm-1 between \(p^{(r)}\) and \(p^{(r-1)}\) is less than the tolerance argument tol and outputs \(p^{(r)}\).

References

Yuille, A.L., Rangarajan, A. (2001). The concave-convex procedure (CCCP). In Proceedings of the Neural Information Processing Systems 2001, Vancouver, BC, Canada, 9–14, December 2001, 1033-1040. doi:10.5555/2980539.2980672

Nielsen, F. (2020). On a Generalization of the Jensen-Shannon Divergence and the Jensen-Shannon Centroid. Entropy, 22, 221–244. doi:10.3390/e22020221

See also

arithcent(), geomcent(), jcent(), catdist.

Examples

p <- igccatdist(dbinom(0:4, size = 4, prob = 0.5))
q <- igccatdist(rep(1/5, times = 5))
r <- igccatdist(c(0.3, 0.4, 0.1, 0.1, 0.1))
matp <- matrix(c(p, q, r), nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE)
matptest <- igcmatcatdistn(p = matp)
jscent(matptest)
#> [1] 0.1821431 0.2907138 0.2210574 0.1863583 0.1197274
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "igccatdistn" "igccatdist" 
#> attr(,"mass")
#> [1] 1
